newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Egana buys 45 pct stake in Thai firm.
newsitem.headline: Egana buys 45 pct stake in Thai firm.

text.p: Egana International (Holdings) Ltd said it acquired a 45 percent stake in a Thai jewellery maker and distributor Keimothai Ltd, and planned to spin off its jewellery operations in a separate listing in the future.
It gave no detail on the investment amount involved in the Keimothai acquisition. Company officials were not immediately available for comment.

Egana said Keimothai was 92.5 held by its founder, Kurt Keller, and 7.5 percent by an unidentified Thai national. Keller will hold 47.5 percent of Keimothai after the deal while the Thai national's stake will remain unchanged at 7.5 percent.
Keimothai engages in manufacturing and distribution of fine jewellery, with the right to sell 20 percent of its products in Thailand. Its customers include Christ Holding GmbH and Tiffany.

Egana said the purchase will expand the geographical coverage of its jewellery products to Thailand and strengthen its relationship with Christ Holding, which has a jewellery and timepiece retail chain in Germany and Switzerland.
Egana said it intends to hold Keimothai as a long-term investment and will extend a corporate guarantee to the extent of HK$10 million for Keimothai as working capital.
Egana said it would appoint Keller as an advisor to the holding company it will set up for its jewellery operations.
Keller is also granted a right to take up to five percent interest in the jewelery division group upon success of its flotation in a recognised stock exchange, it said.
